correctness.rationale: Exact step responses were integrated analytically. The dilogarithmic derivative is positive on (0,1/5], and the second derivative is negative on [1/5,1); with the terminal negative derivative this yields exactly one global maximizer. The distributional BV step-measure representation and positivity/constant preservation give the sharp all-BV bound, and equality support is forced to the unique jump. Reflection proves the other composition. The actual standalone checker passed 59 formula-versus-quadrature comparisons and 65 signed multi-jump tests. Remaining limits: only real unweighted BV inputs and one alternation; finite tests are not substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The canonical first alternating pair of forward/backward finite-interval averages is a natural smoothing benchmark. A complete sharp real-BV-to-L1 coefficient and uniquely positioned equality jumps quantify non-obvious worsening after adding a positive averaging step: 0.41050749 exceeds 1/e. The result separates alternating composition from both one-sided iteration and convex mixing, giving a useful precise worst-case discontinuity test for analysis of iterative averaging.
